Twisting the specified frame once leaves the Wall conditions unchanged, but the resulting frame cannot extend over the disk. The smallest missing prerequisite is that each specified frame equal the input immersion's induced extending frame, or the conclusion must be weakened.

The theorem explicitly allows nonzero relative framing obstruction (Facts & Assumptions and §10.1) yet concludes framed embedded disks preserving those boundary frames (§§11–12). The input generic immersion has its own induced extending boundary framing; an independently twisted nonextending frame cannot be carried by an embedded disk. Require zero relative obstruction for each disk or reconcile the conclusion. This is a substantive prerequisite gap.

Outside this batch, its open-problem statement asks for replacement disks with exactly the same framed boundary circles while the referenced data definition admits nonextending boundary frames. Such inputs already obstruct that conclusion for framing reasons; the owner should reconcile the formulation with the missing extension prerequisite.
